newsitem.title: USA: Dollar gains against yen in thin post-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar gains against yen in thin post-holiday trade.

text.p: The dollar climbed to its highest level in more than 3-1/2 years against the yen Thursday as the Japanese currency took a beating after stock prices tumbled again in Tokyo.

The dollar was boosted by strength in stock markets at home, where the Dow Jones industrial average rose for the seventh consecutive session. With most markets in Europe still closed for the Christmas holiday, trading was light, currency dealers said.

"We're in holiday mode, it's very thin and there's very little incentive to be involved at this point unless you really have to be," said Paul Park, vice president and dollar-yen trader at Pittsburgh-based Mellon Bank.

Trading was busy in Tokyo though after Japan's cabinet approved a draft 1997 budget late on Wednesday calling for a tax increase and a delay in a corporate tax cut, worrying investors that the fledgling economic recovery may be derailed.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares plunged more than 700 points at one point before rebounding to close down 257.83 points at 19,291.58.
"The dollar's rise against the yen came on the back of the drop in the Nikkei," said Mellon's Park.
"The knee-jerk reaction has just been to buy dollars against yen. It's the easiest money out there right now and I think it will continue to attract investors," he said.

The dollar touched 115.08 yen in Tokyo trading, its highest level since April 1993. The dollar stood at 114.95 yen late in New York trading, up from 114.47 late on Tuesday. New York markets were closed for Christmas on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expect weakness in Japan's stock market to continue to weigh on the yen, which is hurt by sales of Japanese stocks that tend to decrease demand for yen.

Comments from a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official helped cap the dollar's gains against the yen. The official told Reuters that Japan's monetary authorities did not welcome wild currency fluctuations and were keeping a close watch on developments in the foreign exchange market.
Dealers interpreted the remarks as meaning that Japanese officials would frown on a further decline in their currency against the dollar.
"With dollar/yen reaching new cycle highs it was enough to introduce a little bit of caution into the market," said Bob Lynch, senior currency analyst at MMS International.
Dealers said strength in the domestic stock market helped the dollar. But thin post-Christmas trading confined the currency to a tight ranges vs. most major currencies.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 23.83 points to 6,546.68, about a point shy of the record 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25.
The dollar ended at 1.5541 German marks, off slightly from Tuesday's 1.5565 marks. The dollar settled at 1.3450 Swiss francs, little changed from 1.3455 on Tuesday.
Elsewhere, the British pound edged higher to $1.6740 from $1.6725 on Tuesday. The dollar fell slightly to Canadian $1.3638 from C$1.3650.
